title: Region-aware Proof Matrix and Evidence Collector Runbook for SOC 2 / ISO27001
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a unified, region-aware 'proof matrix' that maps SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls to automated evidence collectors and retention policies, plus a runbook for onboarding new controls and regions. This will standardize what artifacts we collect (logs, config snapshots, access attestations), where they are stored (regional buckets / lockboxes), and how long they are retained to satisfy jurisdictional requirements.
acceptance_criteria: A documented proof matrix that maps at least 30 core SOC 2/ISO controls to concrete evidence artifact types and automated collectors
A runbook with step-by-step onboarding for a new region that includes registry of storage locations, retention settings, and KMS key bindings
A working prototype collector that produces timestamped evidence bundles and stores them in the configured region-specific vault
Retention settings applied and validated for at least two regions with differing retention laws (e.g., EU vs US) and a verification test that simulates data deletion requests
Integration points documented for Console export (CSV/ZIP) and compliance dashboard showing evidence coverage per control
steps: Survey existing control mappings in Confluence and the evidence index to extract current artifact types
Design 'proof matrix' schema (flat CSV/JSON) that includes control ID, artifact types, collector name, storage locale, retention policy, verification frequency
Prototype a lightweight collector that pulls snapshots from the runtime (config, route policies, token usage) and packages them into time-bound artifacts
Implement regional storage mapping with KMS key aliasing and immutable retention flags where required
Create runbook pages: onboarding checklist, run commands, rollback steps, access review steps
Coordinate with Engineering for collector webhooks and with Security for KMS access reviews
Run validation tests for retention and cross-region proof replication/fallback
progress_updates: 2026-02-05: Kickoff meeting with Security, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed on scope: focus first on evidence artifacts for 'Access Controls', 'Change Management', 'Logging'
2026-02-18: Inventory complete for existing artifact producers. Found 12 automated sources and 8 manual artifacts requiring operator capture
2026-02-27: Draft of proof matrix schema shared in Confluence (link below). Seeking feedback on required fields and extension points
2026-03-04: Engineering owner assigned to prototype collector (ENG-21098). Prototype will emit signed bundles to S3-compatible regional buckets
2026-03-10: Security reviewed proposed KMS alias pattern and retention flag approach; minor edits requested for key rotation docs
decisions: Use a single canonical proof matrix format (CSV + JSON schema) to remain tool-agnostic for exports and imports
Evidence bundles will be SHA256-signed and include metadata headers: collector_id, control_ids, region, timestamp, schema_version

Retention policies are enforced at storage layer using region-specific retention flags where available; when not available, retention will be implemented by scheduled delete jobs with retention-proof logs
Collectors should prefer deterministic, idempotent snapshots to make verification and re-ingestion simpler
risks: Legal/regulatory edge cases: some jurisdictions may require immutable custody or stricter lockbox controls beyond our storage choices
Operational complexity: mapping every control to an automated collector may be infeasible; some artifacts will remain manual and need operator SLAs
Performance: collectors taking large snapshots could impact runtime unless throttled/async
Cross-region verification: ensuring evidence parity during failover needs careful testing
notes: This ticket should drive a reusable pattern: schema + collector + runbook. Aim to make the proof matrix importable by the Console so customers can download region-specific evidence bundles for audits.
